drafted_from: workflow:buy-and-deliver's row in tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json (its input schema, steps and submit shapes)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:buy-and-deliver for 50 paper bakery boxes and a clipboard, delivered to Sunrise Bakery by Friday 9 AM; ask me with the price before ordering."

lists.label: Waiting on you
lists.holds: One thing only the person can finish, with why, how they finish it and what was tried first.

values.why: The market only accepts a form signed by the shop owner.
values.only_you_because: A signature is your own consent
values.tried: Filled in every other field from the shop facts; the signature line stayed empty.
values.done_when: The signed form is sent back

values.what: Tap to order 50 paper bakery boxes for 41.50
values.why: The plan says to bring boxes by Saturday.
values.tried: Found the store, built the order up to payment.

instructions: 1. Pour the example rows into the list where you keep things that need your approval (see pour), or make list:waiting-on-you from them.
2. Say "Run workflow:buy-and-deliver" with items, deliver_to and by.
3. The AI works find, ask and order: it finds where each item can arrive by then with the total price, puts one row on your Waiting on you list whose tap orders it, and orders only after your tap.
4. Tap the row to order; read the order id it records, or the route buttons for a pickup.

worked_examples.title: The price becomes one tap on the Waiting on you list
worked_examples.ask: Buy boxes and a clipboard for Friday.
worked_examples.given: The find step answered {"where":"Example Packaging Supply online store (an account the person has)","price":"41.50 total with delivery"}. The ask step puts one row on the Waiting on you list with what, where and the price; nothing is ordered before the tap. Read from the ask step of the workflow row.
worked_examples.hands_back: The submit shape of step ask: {"asked":true,"waiting_row":"record:waiting-on-you:order-bakery-boxes"}

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
